result.question: For our transformer fleet planning, take the known failure modes for a transformer and tell me which of them we can actually watch on Transformer 1 at site MAIN with the channels it reports today. For each failure mode, list the two or three most diagnostic sensors among hydrogen, methane, ethane, ethylene, acetylene, co, co2, oxygen, nitrogen, dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oti, oti_a, oti_t, ati, il1, il2, il3 and inut. Then mark each mode as 'well covered', 'partially covered' or 'blind', based on whether those sensors have data in the available window. Only list sensors that genuinely discriminate that mode, not ones that just correlate generally. If a mode's key sensor exists but has no values in the window, count the mode as blind rather than covered, and suggest which offline test or extra sample would close the gap.
result.answer:
**Fleet planning: Transformer 1 @ MAIN — failure-mode observability**

Data window: 5 records, 2024-01-15 → 2024-01-19. All 30 reported channels, including every gas, oil-quality and thermal sensor you listed, have non-null values in this window. Status below is based on whether each mode's genuinely discriminative sensors (from your list) have live data.

| Failure mode | Most diagnostic sensors (from your list) | Coverage | Gap to close |
|---|---|---|---|
| Partial Discharge in Oil | hydrogen, acetylene, methane | **Well covered** — all three populated; PD shows as rising H₂ with minor C₂H₂ | None |
| Thermal Fault — Oil Overheating | oti, oti_a, oti_t, ethylene | **Well covered** — OTI with alarm/trip flags plus C₂H₄, the classic >300 °C marker | None |
| Thermal Fault — Core/Winding | ethylene, ethane, co | **Well covered** — C₂H₄/C₂H₆ ratios distinguish core/winding hot spots; CO for involvement of solid insulation | None |
| Low-Energy Arcing (Sparking) | hydrogen, acetylene, methane | **Well covered** — H₂ + C₂H₂ pattern is discriminative | None |
| High-Energy Arcing | acetylene, ethylene, hydrogen | **Well covered** — significant C₂H₂ (often >50 ppm) with C₂H₄ and H₂ | None |
| Tap Changer Mechanical Wear | acetylene, ethane, hydrogen | **Partially covered** — gases detect arcing/wear, but note: if this is a diverter-switch OTC with a separate compartment, main-tank DGA won't see it | Periodic DGA of the selector/diverter-switch compartment oil (or online sampling valve on the OTC) to close the gap |
| Oil Contamination / Moisture Ingress | dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v, oxygen | **Well covered** — IFT and dielectric strength fall directly with moisture/particulates; O₂ with nitrogen indicates open-breather moisture ingress | (water_content is also reported and would sharpen this) |
| Cellulose Insulation Ageing | co, co2, oti | **Well covered** — CO/CO₂ ratio plus sustained winding/oil temperature; data present | Periodic furan (2-FAL) analysis would quantify DP, but coverage is adequate |
| Oil Dielectric Degradation | dbds, dielectric_rigidity, interfacial_v | **Well covered** — DBDS + breakdown voltage + IFT are the direct discriminators for oil oxidation/contamination | None |

**Summary:** 8 of 9 modes are **well covered**; **Tap Changer Mechanical Wear** is **partially covered** (main-tank DGA is indirect — add OTC-compartment oil sampling). No mode is **blind**, since all key sensors exist and carry values in the 2024-01-15→19 window. One planning caveat: the window is only 5 daily records, so trend-based discrimination (essential for thermal and arcing modes) is thin — a longer monitoring history or more frequent DGA sampling would strengthen early detection.
